title: Signal Zero — YC Demo Day Founder Hero
description: A tightly centered pitch hero built around the Y-Combinator demo-day format: a punchy problem statement crown, bold company name, one-line product descriptor, and a saturated orange accent strip anchoring the batch tag and date at the bottom. Nothing competes with the message.
philosophy: This template exists for the 60-second first impression — the moment before a founder utters a single word. It refuses sidebars, decorative texture, and any visual element that does not directly answer 'What problem do you solve, and who are you?' The vertical symmetry is deliberate: it forces every line to earn its position and signals the quiet confidence of a founder who does not need to shout. The room is full of investors who have seen a thousand decks; the only currency here is clarity.
goodFor: Y-Combinator and accelerator demo-day opening slides
Company name and one-liner reveals at the top of a pitch deck
Startup pitch competitions with strict per-slide time limits
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring data density
Multi-column feature or pricing comparison slides
Academic research presentations expecting citation-level detail
Brand campaigns dependent on full-bleed photography or illustration
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide embodies the quiet authority of a founder who needs no decoration — just the message. Compositionally austere and vertically symmetrical, every element earns its position by surviving a ruthless edit, floating in deliberate negative space that amplifies rather than dilutes. The saturated accent strip at the base functions as a visual full stop: it grounds the composition and signals institutional credibility without competing for attention. Avoid texture overlays, illustrative elements, gradient washes, or any asymmetric motif — the power is in the stillness.

examples.layoutNotes: Single-column centered grid with generous outer margin (~10%) on all four sides — no edge-to-edge bleed except the bottom accent strip. Problem statement sits as a crown element in the upper third, separated from the company name by a deliberate pocket of negative space. Company name occupies the true visual center and is the highest-weight element on the canvas; the one-line product descriptor sits immediately below it at a significantly reduced scale, separated by weight contrast alone — no rule lines. A full-width accent strip bleeds wall-to-wall at the very bottom, housing the batch tag and date flush-centered in a single tight row, acting as the sole horizontal anchor in an otherwise vertical hierarchy.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a single well-rehearsed sentence delivered to a room of investors — spare, deliberate, and slightly kinetic. Compositional rhythm is vertically anchored: one dominant idea occupies the visual center of gravity, with minimal satellite text orbiting above and below rather than flanking it sideways. The mood is controlled urgency without ornamentation — the kind of quiet that commands attention before a word is spoken. Avoid texture, illustration, or any secondary panel that competes with the primary claim.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with active content locked to cols 3–10, preserving the template's centered spine. A hairline rule separates a short section label at the top from the primary content block — expressed as one dominant stat callout or a capped three-item list with a terse descriptor beneath each point. No header band at top; the saturated accent strip persists at the bottom edge carrying slide number or section tag. Hierarchy is achieved through weight contrast alone, with no decorative dividers or icons.
